IncidentBot: INCIDENT: p99 streaming latency above SLO in us-west-2 (p99 ~ 1.8s, SLO 1.0s). Paging #eng-sre and oncall. incident_id=INC-20260410-024
Priya R: ack, I'm oncall. checking dashboards and recent deploys. any signal of config changes? :eyes:
Alice K: graphs show a sharp jump at 2026-04-10T15:03:00Z — p95 went 420ms -> 750ms, p99 900ms -> 1.8s. streaming stalls correlate with contbatch queue depth. link: https://grafana/reports/abc123
Ben T: looking at scheduler logs — contbatch scheduler lingered while packing mixed seq lengths. backlog spike on packer thread. seqlen histogram shows a heavy tail (many > 2k tokens). this amplifies batching tail.
Alice K: quick query:
```
// recent percentiles (us-west-2, streaming)
p95 = 0.75
p99 = 1.82
error_rate = 0.06
```
Ben T: suspect mixed-seqlen amplification + KV-cache churn on hot prefixes. also seeing preemption delays when streaming attempts to interleave with large batch jobs.
Priya R: customer impact? which tenants hit first?
Alice K: top impacted: alpha-app (40% timeouts on streaming), search-svc (degraded latency), chat-sms (sporadic stalls). roughly 2% of total requests, but concentrated on high seqlen workloads.
Ben T: immediate mitigations I suggest: 1) reduce max_batch_size on contbatch-usw2 pool 64 -> 32 2) enable pack_shed for seqlen > 1024 to avoid packing huge sequences with small ones 3) route free-tier streaming to fallback fast-stream variant (lower latency, lower model quality) while we stabilize.
Priya R: Marc H can you run the runbook steps? I'll coordinate customer comms and keep the page updated. @Marc H
Marc H: on it. running the first command now:
```
# reduce max_batch_size on pool
rbctl pool set contbatch-usw2 --max-batch 32 && rbctl pool annotate contbatch-usw2 "mitigation: reduce batch size due to tail amplification"
```
Marc H: applied config change, returns OK. triggering rolling restart of packer pods (12 pods):
```
kubectl rollout restart deploy/contbatch-packer -n inference-usw2
rolling restart started for 12 pods, expected 3-4 min to drain
```
Marc H: also enabled pack_shed for seqlen>1024 on the packer flags. toggled scheduler fairness to strict mode to avoid long-linger packing.
OpsBot: MONITOR: 5m window update — p95=0.62s, p99=0.98s, error_rate=0.015.
Priya R: nice, numbers are trending back under SLO. continuing to watch 30m. I'll prepare a short customer note for alpha-app and search-svc.
Ben T: follow-up: need a long-term fix — adaptive batch sizing by seqlen buckets and KV cache pinning to avoid eviction hotspots. filing ticket ENG-PLT-589 for design.
Alice K: I'm capturing the logs and saving slices for postmortem. also will collect a sample prompt set that caused amplification.
Priya R: handoff: I'm handing oncall to Marc H in 15m since mitigation is applied. Marc, you'll own the escalation channel.
Marc H: acknowledged. keeping watch. if p99 creeps above 1.2s I'll rollback the fairness toggle and revert batch size and try alternate packing policy.
OpsBot: ALERT: incident_id=INC-20260410-024 marked RESOLVED at 2026-04-10T15:11:00Z — p99 back within SLO for 10m rolling window.
Priya R: thanks team — good coordination. I'll draft a postmortem and customer impact summary. assigning follow-ups:
- ENG-PLT-589: adaptive batching design (Ben T)
- ENG-SRE-342: KV cache pinning experiment (Alice K)
- COMM-134: customer notes for alpha-app/search-svc (Priya R)
Marc H: leaving monitoring on; will escalate if it reappears.
IncidentBot: INCIDENT CLOSED: INC-20260410-024 (latency spike mitigated).
